name: Few-Shot Prompting
description: In-context learning: give the model a few input-output examples in the prompt; the technique introduced alongside GPT-3 (Brown et al., 2020).

name: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
description: Elicit step-by-step reasoning with intermediate rationales; large gains on arithmetic and symbolic tasks (Wei et al., 2022).

name: Zero-Shot Chain-of-Thought
description: Append 'Let's think step by step' to trigger reasoning with no examples (Kojima et al., 2022).

name: Self-Consistency
description: Sample multiple reasoning paths and take the majority answer; improves over greedy CoT decoding (Wang et al., 2022).

name: Least-to-Most Prompting
description: Decompose a problem into easier subproblems and solve them sequentially (Zhou et al., 2022).

name: Generated Knowledge Prompting
description: First generate relevant knowledge statements, then condition the answer on them; helps commonsense reasoning (Liu et al., 2022).

name: Scratchpad
description: Let the model write intermediate computation into a 'scratchpad' before answering (Nye et al., 2021).

name: ReAct
description: Interleave reasoning traces with actions (search, tools); synergizes chain-of-thought with tool use (Yao et al., 2022).

name: Program-Aided Language Models (PAL)
description: Offload computation to a Python interpreter: the model writes code, the runtime executes it (Gao et al., 2022).

name: Plan-and-Solve Prompting
description: First devise a plan dividing the task into subtasks, then execute it; strengthens zero-shot CoT (Wang et al., 2023).

name: ART
description: Automatic multi-step reasoning and tool use: pause generation at tool calls, resume with the outputs (Paranjape et al., 2023).

name: ReWOO
description: Decouple reasoning from observations: plan all tool calls upfront (planner/worker/solver), cutting token cost (Xu et al., 2023).

name: Tree of Thoughts
description: Search over coherent thought units with lookahead and backtracking for deliberate problem solving (Yao et al., 2023).

name: Graph of Thoughts
description: Generalize tree search to arbitrary graph topologies over thought units for elaborate problems (Besta et al., 2023).

name: Self-Refine
description: Iterative refinement loop: generate, self-critique with feedback, refine (Madaan et al., 2023).

name: Reflexion
description: Verbal reinforcement learning: agents reflect on failures in natural language and retry (Shinn et al., 2023).

name: Active Prompting
description: Select the most uncertain examples for human annotation to build better few-shot CoT sets (Diao et al., 2023).

name: Complexity-Based Prompting
description: Prefer few-shot examples with more reasoning steps; complex prompts transfer better (Fu et al., 2022).

name: Contrastive Chain-of-Thought
description: Show both valid and invalid reasoning demonstrations so the model learns what mistakes to avoid (Chia et al., 2023).

name: Directional Stimulus Prompting
description: A small tunable model generates hints ('stimuli') that steer a frozen LLM (Li et al., 2023).

name: Analogical Prompting
description: Ask the model to recall analogous problems and solve them first, then tackle the target (Yasunaga et al., 2023).

name: Multi-Agent Debate
description: Several model instances debate with self-generated arguments; improves factuality and reasoning (Du et al., 2023).

name: Meta-Prompting
description: One LM acts as conductor, delegating subtasks to tailored 'expert' instances of itself; zero-shot and task-agnostic (Suzgun & Kalai, 2024).

name: Prompt Chaining
description: Split a task into sequential LLM steps where each step's output feeds the next; a core production pattern in the vendor guides.

name: DSPy
description: Stanford framework for programming LMs: composable modules (signatures) plus optimizers instead of hand-written prompts.

name: LangChain
description: Framework for LLM apps: prompt templates, chains, agents, and a large integration ecosystem.

name: Guidance
description: Control language interleaving generation with programming logic: regex, CFGs, and structured control flow.

name: LMQL
description: Query language for LLMs with constraints, scripting, and decoding control (ETH SRI).

name: Outlines
description: Structured text generation: constrain decoding with regex, JSON schema, or grammars.

name: Instructor
description: Structured LLM outputs in Python: Pydantic-validated responses with automatic retries.

name: BAML
description: Typed prompt functions: write prompts as functions with schemas; Boundary's LLM-function language.

name: ell
description: Lightweight prompt-engineering library: prompts as versioned, testable Python functions.

name: APPL
description: Prompt programming language: embed natural-language prompts in Python with async parallelization and tracing.

name: marvin
description: Prefect's AI engineering framework: typed, testable LLM functions via Python decorators.

name: Semantic Kernel
description: Microsoft's SDK for wiring LLMs into apps: semantic functions, planners, and plugins.

name: Mirascope
description: Typed, provider-agnostic LLM calls in Python with prompt templates built from type hints.

name: TypeChat
description: Microsoft's TypeScript library for building typed natural-language interfaces.

name: Promptfoo
description: Open-source LLM eval toolkit: assertions, red-teaming, and CI-ready prompt test runs.

name: LangSmith
description: LangChain's platform for prompt iteration: prompt hub/versioning, tracing, and evals.

name: Langfuse
description: Open-source LLM engineering platform: prompt management and versioning, tracing, analytics.

name: Helicone
description: Open-source LLM observability proxy: request logging, caching, rate limits, and evals.

name: W&B Weave
description: Weights & Biases toolkit for tracing, versioning, and evaluating LLM calls.

name: PromptLayer
description: Prompt registry with versioning and release labels, request logging, and evals; Python/JS SDKs.

name: Vellum
description: Prompt playground, versioning, and workflow builder for production LLM apps.

name: OpenAI Playground
description: OpenAI's hosted console for iterating on prompts across models and parameters.

name: Anthropic Workbench
description: Anthropic Console's prompt IDE: iterate, compare, and test prompts.

name: Automatic Prompt Engineer (APE)
description: LLMs as human-level prompt engineers: generate and select instructions automatically (Zhou et al., 2022).

name: OPRO
description: Optimization by PROmpting: use an LLM as the optimizer, described in natural language (Yang et al., 2023).

name: Promptbreeder
description: Self-referential self-improvement: evolve both task-prompts and mutation-prompts (Fernando et al., 2023).

name: EvoPrompt
description: Connect LLMs with evolutionary algorithms for discrete prompt optimization (Guo et al., 2023).

name: ProTeGi
description: Automatic prompt optimization with textual 'gradient descent' and beam search (Pryzant et al., 2023).

name: TextGrad
description: Automatic 'differentiation' via text: backpropagate natural-language feedback through compound AI systems (Yuksekgonul et al., 2024).

name: PromptWizard
description: Microsoft's task-aware optimizer: self-evolving critique-and-synthesis loop over instructions and examples (Agarwal et al., 2024). Code: microsoft/PromptWizard.

name: DSPy Optimizers
description: Programmatic prompt optimization (COPRO, MIPRO): compile declarative LM pipelines against a metric.

name: OpenAI Evals
description: OpenAI's framework for evaluating LLMs and LLM systems with YAML-defined evals.

name: LM Evaluation Harness
description: EleutherAI's standard harness for few-shot evaluation of language models.

name: HELM
description: Stanford CRFM's holistic evaluation of language models across scenarios and metrics.

name: PromptBench
description: Microsoft's benchmark for prompt robustness: attacks, defenses, and prompt variations. (Archived.)

name: DeepEval
description: Open-source LLM evaluation framework: unit-test-style evals with 14+ research-backed metrics.

name: Chain-of-Thought Hub
description: Benchmark suite measuring chain-of-thought reasoning across math, science, and symbolic tasks.

name: OpenAI Prompt Engineering Guide
description: OpenAI's official playbook: the six strategies for getting better results.

name: Anthropic Prompt Engineering Docs
description: Anthropic's Claude docs: prompt structure, chaining prompts, and long-context tips.

name: Google Prompt Engineering Whitepaper
description: Lee Boonstra's 68-page practitioner whitepaper (Google/Kaggle): techniques from zero-shot to ReAct.

name: Learn Prompting
description: Free, open-source course covering beginner to advanced prompting.

name: Prompt Engineering Guide (DAIR.AI)
description: Community reference for prompting techniques, papers, and model-specific notes.

name: Lil'Log: Prompt Engineering
description: Lilian Weng's deep, well-referenced tour of prompting research.

name: A Prompt Pattern Catalog
description: Reusable prompt patterns for ChatGPT: personas, recipes, templates, and games (White et al., 2023).

name: Brex Prompt Engineering Guide
description: Brex's public playbook: structured outputs, grounding, and production prompting.

name: Awesome ChatGPT Prompts
description: Community-curated collection of ChatGPT system prompts across roles and tasks.

name: OpenAI Cookbook
description: OpenAI's example code and guides, including many prompt-engineering patterns.

name: Pre-train, Prompt, and Predict
description: Foundational survey of prompting methods in NLP (Liu et al., 2021).

name: A Systematic Survey of Prompt Engineering in Large Language Models
description: 44 techniques across application areas with per-task performance summaries (2024).

name: The Prompt Report
description: Taxonomy of 58 prompting techniques from 1,500+ papers plus meta-analysis (Schulhoff et al., 2024).

name: Why Johnny Can't Prompt
description: CHI 2023 study: how non-experts actually design prompts - and fail (Zamfirescu-Pereira et al.).

name: DSPy: Compiling Declarative Language Model Calls into Self-Improving Pipelines
description: The DSPy paper: separate program from prompt, optimize programmatically (Khattab et al., 2023).

name: Prompting Is Programming (LMQL)
description: A query language for LLMs with constraints and control flow (Beurer-Kellner et al., 2022).

name: A Systematic Survey of Prompt Engineering on Vision-Language Foundation Models
description: Prompting for Flamingo, CLIP, Stable Diffusion and friends (Gu et al., 2023).

name: Indirect Prompt Injection
description: 'Not what you've signed up for': compromising real-world LLM-integrated apps via indirect injection (Greshake et al., 2023).

name: Simon Willison: Prompt Injection Series
description: Ongoing field notes on prompt-injection attacks and defenses.

name: OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications
description: Security risks for LLM apps, starting with LLM01 prompt injection.
